title: Map board RF paths and applicable errata
description:
Map each selected board's oscillator, RF switches, filters, matching, antennas and chip/modem-firmware errata from primary documents. Distinguish board coverage from silicon tuning range. Assess applicability of published wake/calibration and adjacent-channel-power limitations using exact revisions.

HPC8 execution policy: Code, test, or schema changes require three independent correctness, security, and robustness reviews; file and fix all findings and re-review. Use independent oracles, never weakened legacy tests or self-generated expected results. Preserve upstream Yggdrasil addressing, radio-owned identity, best-effort custody, baseline SCHC, and the human-only OSCORE/EDHOC security edit bar. External actions, hardware/RF operations, and port access require scoped explicit permission and applicable bench safety checks. Research may conclude no-go; an authorization gate requires affirmative, recorded approval for its actual scope. Dependency closure and decomposition are not permission. No speculative activation, including deferred portability or experimental modes.
design: Read-only documentary analysis. Reuse existing project-LICHEN-h7t5.7.5 and its .13 RF-switch/TCXO work when that board is selected, respecting owner-reserved scope. Do not create duplicate bring-up implementation, open ports or change board settings.
acceptance_criteria: Schematic/BOM/vendor evidence supports each claimed RF path and erratum applicability, or marks it unknown. Do not assume all LR1110 units share a firmware defect or that all SX1262 boards cover the full band. Produce measurement hypotheses and equipment-specific limitations, not qualification results.
